submission.natural_language_explanation: Ignoring each text's first token (where it has a floor), this pole is a retrospective lexical detector: it fires on the current token at 0.4-1.5x the scan scale when the token is a common word of public/collective life, work and media (care, health, staff, press, media, art, land, train, protest, benefit, rights, energy, value, program, result, war, team, population, 'thing'), a light transfer/exchange or motion verb (give/gave/given/gives, sell/sold, offer, hold/held, go/went/going, come, bring, want, help), or one of the very common quantifier/discourse words (not, most, any, least, still, ever, never, good, best, sure), and it fires more weakly (0.15-0.4x) on the rest of that same general vocabulary (city, council, authority, mayor, vote, law, news, power, radio, plan, women, man, take, put, keep, public, police). It sits at the GELU floor (0.00 of scale) on personal, domestic and natural-kind vocabulary (father, mother, child, family, friend, house, tree, table, cup, doctor, bird, cat, dog, book, garden, village), on perception, cognition and manipulation verbs (see, hear, watch, touch, follow, lead, leave, own, open, close, change, grow, clean, cut, fill, drop, lift, pull, build, sort, mix, count, arrange, remember, measure, save, buy, pay), and on longer abstract or institutional labels (society, community, culture, method, system, process, contract, economy, business, industry, history, question, court, minister, policy, budget, report, statement, paper); the split is lexical and graded rather than syntactic or sense-based, so 'give' fires while 'see' does not, 'sell' fires while 'buy' does not, and 'staff' fires while 'doctor' does not.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The hospital trust said extra staff would help the night shift.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: 'staff' and 'help' are claimed high-fire words placed in a new hospital-administration context unlike any top example, so the lexical hypothesis predicts a peak on them.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: To start the machine, press the green button twice and wait for the light.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout testing the claim that the split is lexical rather than sense-based: 'press' here is the button-pressing verb, not news media, and the hypothesis predicts it fires anyway.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: They went to the market and sold the last of the crop before noon.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: 'went' and 'sold' are claimed motion/exchange verbs in a market setting, predicted to fire despite the genre differing from the top examples.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Voters were told the new program would bring more benefits to the region.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positive holdout: 'program', 'bring' and 'benefit' in a political-news sentence, predicted to fire as common public/work vocabulary.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The town had drawn its water from the same well for a hundred years. When the pumps began to fail, the engineers were sent out to inspect the pipes under the square. They found rust in the joints and clay in the filters, and they warned that the supply could fail again in winter. The board met on a Tuesday and asked for a second well to be dug on the hill behind the church. Work began in spring. The new pipes were laid in a trench along the lane, and the old well was capped with concrete. By the end of summer the taps ran clear again, and the health inspector signed off on the new supply.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Long-context positive holdout: the only claimed word, 'health', sits deep in a paragraph of otherwise unlisted neutral vocabulary, and a token-level lexical detector should still peak on it.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
def flush(sock):
    # give the peer two seconds to read before the buffer closes
    sock.write(FIN)
    time.sleep(2)
adversarial_test_results.detail: Cross-genre positive holdout: 'give' appears inside a code comment, an unusual position and genre, and the hypothesis predicts the token fires regardless of context.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Her father sat at the table with a cup of tea and watched the birds in the garden.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative: the content is domestic and natural-kind (father, table, cup, birds, garden) with the perception verb 'watched', all on the hypothesis's GELU-floor list, so it predicts no measured fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The minister denied the report, and the committee will question the policy and the budget.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative: the same public-affairs topic as the activating examples but expressed only in longer institutional labels (minister, report, question, policy, budget), which the hypothesis says sit at the floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I can see the river from my room, and I can hear it at night.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative: perception verbs 'see' and 'hear' plus natural-kind 'river' with no claimed trigger; the hypothesis puts perception verbs at the floor, so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She opened the box, cut the string, and pulled out a small book.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative: manipulation verbs 'opened', 'cut' and 'pulled' with 'book', all on the hypothesis's floor list, so no measured token should fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Care for the garden was left to the family.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Positional hard negative: the only claimed word 'care' opens the text where the first-token floor is not measured, and every remaining content word (garden, left, family) is on the floor list, so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The pressure on the seal was too high, so the valve failed.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative morphological near-miss: 'pressure' contains the letters of the claimed word 'press' but is its own common token the hypothesis does not list, so a token-level detector should stay down.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The doctor read the report and left the office before the meeting.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative built on the hypothesis's own contrast case: the workplace topic remains (office, meeting), but the exact floor tokens ' doctor' and ' report' replace staff and media, and the hypothesis says 'staff fires while doctor does not', so predicted inactive.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: History shows that a system of industry and business changes through trial and error.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative: dense longer abstract and institutional labels (history, system, industry, business) with the floor verb 'changes', which the hypothesis predicts sit at the GELU floor.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The cupboard was bare; the shelves were covered in dust.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative delimiter control matched to the punctuation of several top examples: the word 'cupboard' splits into the tokens ' cup' | 'board', and ' cup' is an exact floor word, so the hypothesis still predicts inactivity and a fire would implicate the semicolon or the split token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The children played near the house while their mother read a book on the step. The dog slept in the shade, and a bird sang in the tree. Later, the father carried the table onto the grass and they ate together while the sun set behind the village.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Hard negative length control: a long passage of personal and natural-kind vocabulary (child, house, mother, dog, bird, tree, father, table, village) with no claimed token, so the hypothesis predicts inactivity and neither length nor topic alone should move it.
